title: Does anyone else sometimes feel like ai game dev is almost like playing a really hard strategy/sim game itself?
author: Aesthetic-Engine
selftext:
As my current game is starting to take shape after a couple weeks of laying foundation I just had this feeling like what I was doing was sort of feeling like a really deep strategy/sim game. Like it could actually be a game if it had an excellent tutorial. 

It'd be like how they released RPG Maker on the PS1 but on steroids and would require several subscriptions. Has anyone had this thought pass through their heads as they were vibe coding?

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: yeah sort of. I am trying to refine a game demo and it gets even more abstract

replies.author: Aesthetic-Engine
replies.body: It definitely gets more complex once everything begins taking shape. The "game" would need to have a comprehensive understanding of what you're building and would recommend deep research prompts to run to help solve design problems or guide you toward ideas for missing design elements.

replies.author: Aesthetic-Engine
replies.body: Definitely starting to feel that. I think removing the need to memorize syntax sort of offered new difficulty settings/configurations to choose from.

replies.author: Laicbeias
replies.body:
i didn't use it for game dev, but the difficult now scales with the amount of a mess we produce.  
task managment and tracking, testing and playtesting, all that is now kinda the hard part. and when a game really gets big, what they usually just do since their scope is large in nature, llms at some point shit the bed and you burn cash\^\^

comments.author: DatabaseConstant7870
comments.body: It’s like a big sandbox game in a way. Like in all the recent big selling games they’ve all become a way to make games within them. I think these big companies know they can’t keep the creativity going because their motivations are money when a lot of people have really great ideas but will make it on a games sandbox system because it’s easy to use. If there was a tutorial on how to use this “sandbox” it would start by mentioning it has an easier time outside a game engine than within and to look up what all it takes to code a game without a game engine and look at the different languages and why they are best for certain styles of games. Then from there start building with your AI in whatever fits your idea.

replies.author: Aesthetic-Engine
replies.body:
It's true yeah if you look at Roblox it's not the studio's ideas/content that is making them all the money- it's their tools they offered that made game building and modding a lot easier.

It feels like people are just starting to realize agentic game development offers much more creative freedom and opportunities if you can wrap your head around the learning curve and which tools to use.

comments.author: leather-armor
comments.body: I actually feel this way about life as a whole. It's always resource management, and time is also a resource. You need to be smart and strategic. and calculate what you can expect in terms of returned value. You'll even have fail states if you think about it long enough. Anyway, I went way beyond the point... I do understand you though.

comments.author: apisol
comments.body: Yes but I also felt the same about using DAWs, now experiencing the same with agentic coding I feel it's probably just the way you engage with and envision a computer-space and immerse your focus into it that is similar rather than gaming specifically.

replies.author: PuteMorte
replies.body: Making music on a DAW definitely feels like a game, but not a strategy/sim game. At least not to me

replies.author: apisol
replies.body: I dunno they do have some elements shared with Civ/Paradox 4x where earlier decisions all stack on top of each other to eventually provide an outcome. Though I guess it's more like that with a cheat editor or something that lets you retroactively change things that cause cacading effects affecting the outcome.

comments.author: Useful_Use_6170
comments.body: Yeah I learned after so many failed projects lol , it gets easier once u set foundation and get it working then you reskin with assets
